newsitem.title: USA: Ford, UAW bargainers resume contract talks.
newsitem.headline: Ford, UAW bargainers resume contract talks.

text.p: Bargainers for Ford Motor Co. and the United Auto Workers (UAW) resumed negotiations on Saturday in a final push to reach a deal for a new national labor contract before a midnight EDT strike deadline.
Ford officials said they were hopeful a settlement would be reached by the deadline, but optimism earlier in the week for an unprecedented early settlement appeared to be fading.
Talks broke off before midnight on Friday, and members of several key subcommittees arrived at Ford World Headquarters here with suitcases at about 8 a.m. Saturday.
Ford is leading negotiations for the next contracts covering nearly 400,000 UAW hourly workers at Ford, General Motors Corp. and Chrysler Corp.
In the last negotiations in 1993, also led by Ford, it took a marathon 40-hour bargaining session and a nearly 24-hour contract extension to reach a settlement.

Negotiators were working on the toughest issues separating the two sides, including tougher union controls over the company's ability to shift parts work to outside suppliers, according to industry sources.
Other issues said to be still on the table include the possibility of lower wages for newly hired parts plant workers -- a precedent the union has strongly resisted.
On Friday, Ford and the UAW appeared to be leaning toward a traditional three year contract, backing off earlier plans for a pact of four years or longer.

Raises were expected to be two percent per year, as opposed to a three percent base-wage increase in the first year of the current pact, and lump-sum bonuses of three percent in the second and third years. The base-wage increase is considered more beneficial because it is cumulative.
The UAW on Friday extended its contracts with GM and Chrysler, pledging not to strike those automakers while it continued bargaining with Ford.
Meanwhile UAW members at Ford plants around the country continued to prepare for a possible strike if no deal was reached before midnight, making signs and picket duty assignments.
"We're ready to roll," Jerry Klein, president of Local 249 at Ford's Kansas City, Mo. assembly plant. said on Friday. "All we need is the call."
